**Plan**

**Files that differ (read in both places):**
- `/workspace/tenacity/after.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tenacity/after.py`
- `/workspace/tests/test_after.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_after.py`

**What I saw in the current workspace:**
In `/workspace/tenacity/after.py`, the `after_log` function builds a log line by directly pasting the value of `retry_state.seconds_since_start` into the message (line 45). `after_nothing` is unchanged.

In `/workspace/tenacity/__init__.py` (lines 546-548), `seconds_since_start` is a property that returns `None` when `outcome_timestamp` is `None`. Nothing guarantees it is a number when `after_log` runs, so pasting `None` into the number format slot fails.

In `/workspace/tests/test_after.py`, there are only two checks: the default log text and a custom seconds format. No case covers a missing time value.

**What I saw in the reference:**
In `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tenacity/after.py`, `after_log` first reads the time value into a short name, then uses that number only when it is present and shows a question mark when it is missing. `after_nothing` is unchanged.

In `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_after.py`, a new check was added (lines 53-74): it clears the end-of-call time so the time value is `None`, then confirms the log line shows the question mark and no error happens.

**What is missing/wrong for the user today:**
When a finished attempt has no recorded completion time, the log message tool crashes while building its text, because it tries to format a missing value as a number. The user gets an error instead of a log line, and there is no fallback text for the missing seconds.

**Workspace file paths for the Hints section:**
- `/workspace/tenacity/after.py`
- `/workspace/tenacity/__init__.py`
- `/workspace/tests/test_after.py`

**Suggested ticket shape (plain words):**
- Title: log message for a finished attempt breaks when the completion time is missing
- What happens now: the message tries to put a missing time into a number slot and fails
- What should happen: the message shows a question mark in place of the missing seconds, and the log still goes through
- About this project: a library that reruns a failed action and can log when each try finishes
- Problem this solves: a user loses the whole log line (and the run errors) at the exact moment they most need to see that an attempt ended
- What changed: the seconds value is read once; a question mark is shown when there is no time; a new check covers the missing-time case
- Impact: correctness and usability
- User experience: before, a missing time makes the log line blow up; now the line reads with a question mark where the seconds would be
- Hints: the three workspace paths above

I did not check anything in the repo beyond the files above, and I ran no tests.

{"file_path": "/megabit/ticket.md", "content": "# The "finished call" log line breaks when the finish time is unknown

## What happens now
When a retried call finishes, the built-in after-log helper writes a line saying what finished, how long it took, and how many times it was tried. That helper reads the time since the call started. If that time is missing, the helper still tries to show it as a number, which fails. The user gets an error instead of a log line.

## What should happen
When the time since the call started is missing, the line should still be written. It should show a question mark where the number of seconds normally goes, and keep the rest of the words the same, including the call name and the number of tries.

## About this project
This project is a small Python library that reruns a piece of work when it fails, waiting a bit between tries. It also lets people log a line each time a try finishes, so they can watch what happened. Many apps use it to make shaky network calls more reliable.

## Problem this solves
People who watch their logs want every finished try to leave a line. When the finish time is missing, the whole line disappears and an error shows up instead, right when the person is trying to find out what happened.

## What changed
The line now copes with a missing finish time. Where the number of seconds was forced into the words before, the line now shows a question mark instead of failing. A new check covers this missing-time case. The wording of the line for normal runs stays the same.

## Impact
Fewer errors and easier log reading.

## User experience
Before: a call finishes without a recorded finish time, and asking for the finished-call line raises an error, so nothing is written. After: the same call writes the line with a question mark where the seconds would be, showing the call name, the question mark, and which try number it was.

## Hints
- /workspace/tenacity/after.py
- /workspace/tenacity/__init__.py
- /workspace/tests/test_after.py
"}
